_what: Hand-measured regions of interest in photographs of a real ECG printout.
_why: These exist because FR1 (page detection and perspective rectification) and
FR4 (lead segmentation) do not. Every box below is work a finished pipeline
would have to do for itself, done once by a human instead, so that FR3, FR5,
FR6, FR7 and FR8 can be measured on real photographs *now* rather than after
two unbuilt stages land. Treat a number produced with these ROIs as a
measurement of the downstream chain on real ink, never as an end-to-end
result: the hardest part of the problem has been removed by hand.
Fractions are of the DESKEWED image, and the deskew is the shipped default
-angle with expand=True). Fractions rather than pixels because the expand
grows the canvas by an amount that depends on the recovered angle, so pixel
boxes measured in one frame do not transfer to another.
The source images live in data/a30_pics/ and are NOT committed: data/ is
gitignored. This file records what was measured on them so the numbers can
be recomputed by anyone holding the same photographs.

_source.device: Samsung SM-A307FN (Galaxy A30s), the thesis target device
_source.printout: one real clinical 12-lead printout, 3x4 plus a full-width lead II rhythm strip, pale pink grid, a 1 mV calibration pulse printed at the start of each row
_source.printed_from: A print of ecg-image-kit/sample-data/ecg-images/ecg00001.png, confirmed by digitising that PNG and scoring it against these photographs (results/photo/source.csv). It is a public-domain scanned ECG image with NO waveform ground truth -- the kit's ecg-time-series/ folder is empty. 'ecg00001' is a filename, not a PTB-XL ecg_id. Fidelity against a waveform is therefore impossible for this page; use --experiment source, which scores against the clean original instead.

_boxes.paper: gridded paper above the first trace row, used for grid-response measurements that must not see trace ink
_boxes.rhythm: the bottom full-width lead II rhythm strip, the only lead printed as one continuous 10 s trace and therefore the only valid FR5-FR7 input on this page
_boxes.cells: column 1 of the 3x4 block: leads I, II and III, each a 2.5 s window. The x range starts right of the calibration pulse and the printed lead label, both of which would otherwise be traced as signal.

20260921_113331.note: Validated. Paper-band 5 mm comb cv 0.0117; duration anchor gives 20.644 px/mm; all three cells edge-clean. Best repeatability pair with _113327 at PCC 0.847 as-digitised.

20260921_113332.note: Validated. Paper-band comb cv 0.0074; duration anchor 20.596 px/mm. Cells I and II carry slight edge contamination (50 and 15 inked edge pixels); the rhythm strip is edge-clean. Otsu never reaches the correct basin on this frame at any crop tested -- ink stays at 16.9-18.1% where the trace is 3.4%.

20260921_113327.note: Validated, and it was wrongly marked unusable on first reading. An earlier slice-based perspective estimate of 52% was an estimator failure, not perspective: with a comb-regularity guard this is the ONLY frame whose across-page spread is measurable at all, and it is the smallest, 3.48%. Duration anchor 20.776 px/mm. Its rhythm-region comb does fail badly (11.148 px/mm, -44.6% against the duration anchor), which makes it the clearest case for not trusting a comb measured over trace ink. Cells not measured.
20260921_113327.cells_note: Copied from _113331 and NOT individually verified; the two frames are framed almost identically. Check edge cleanliness before quoting a per-cell number from this frame.

20260921_113130.note: 12 MP. Paper-band comb not recoverable. Not resolution-limited: at ~14.7 px/mm it clears the 3 px/mm floor comfortably, and it fails on blur and oblique lighting. EXIF orientation 6.

20260921_113036.note: 12 MP, no 5 mm comb recoverable. EXIF orientation 6.

20260921_113053.note: 12 MP, no 5 mm comb recoverable. EXIF orientation 3.

_measured: Every claim in the per-frame notes comes from results/photo/*.csv.
Where a note and a CSV disagree, the CSV is right: these notes are a
reading aid, not a source. Several first-pass figures quoted during
development did not survive a standardised ROI and are gone.
